Wall Street split on gold following Dems' midterm rout, Main Street bulls emboldened after post-election price rally
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices staged a strong recovery during a volatile week, as an early rebound from last week's sharp selloff gained momentum following the Democratic sweep of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, before a technology-led equity rout and stronger-than-expected U.S. payrolls ate into the precious metal's gains. Spot gold kicked off the week trading at $3,875.21 per ounce on Sunday evening, and the yellow metal quickly pushed higher on Monday as falling oil prices eased inflation concerns and bargain-hunting emerged following the previous week's decline. The recovery stalled Tuesday as stronger U.S. economic data, rising Treasury yields, and a firmer dollar weighed on bullion, with gold briefly retreating below $3,900 before buyers returned. The rally then accelerated Tuesday evening and Wednesday after Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress, raising expectations for legislative gridlock and potentially reduced government borrowing. Treasury yields and the dollar fell sharply as investors reassessed the fiscal outlook, helping gold surge back above $4,000. The advance continued Thursday, when spot prices set their weekly high at $4,147.02 per ounce, before a sharp technology-led equity selloff triggered renewed liquidation across financial markets.

items.titleEn: Sysco Counts on AI Routing and Bidding for $500 Million in Savings
items.summaryEn: Sysco operates 333 distribution centers, serves 670,000 customer locations and drives 4.5 million miles weekly in the United States. It is using AI for routing, supplier bidding and sales recommendations. AI routing improved cases delivered per mile by 2% to 4%, supplier bidding beat savings targets by 30%, and AI360 helped lift Sysco brand mix by 44 basis points. Sysco targets $500 million in savings by fiscal 2029. Wholesale distributors use AI across 35 of 75 business tasks, versus 20 in retail and 22 in construction, according to PYMNTS Intelligence. The research found that 85% of wholesale executives prioritize margins in future AI spending.

items.titleEn: Dems' spending plans ‘would crush the U.S. dollar' and ‘that gives gold a floor' – Phoenix Futures' Grady
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – The incoming Democratic Congress will have no choice but to embrace the AI buildout if they want the revenue to fund their spending priorities – and that spending will likely weaken the dollar and boost gold , according to Kevin Grady, president of Phoenix Futures and Options. Grady said he was surprised to see the market’s initial reaction to the midterm results. “Yesterday was the meltdown, and I was actually surprised at the rally the other day,” he said. “I think that just exacerbated the sell-off yesterday.”

items.titleEn: Gold and the greenback are still at the mercy of Trump and the Fed – Walsh Trading's Weyer
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – The results of the midterm elections were decisive, but the future path of the dollar and gold still remains largely in the hands of the Federal Reserve and the President, according to John Weyer, co-director of commercial hedging at Walsh Trading. Weyer said that while the election removes some uncertainty from the market, it has no impact on the Federal Reserve, and precious metals traders will have to wait and see what the central bank does in December. “The Fed operates differently than we do as participants in the markets,” he said. “They're slow and steady when it comes to data and seeing what happens, and patient. We want to make trades, so we want to play it one way or the other – what does this data mean, what does the election mean? – and I think they’re more inclined to stay on the path they were; they’re going to take in the latest data, the election, digest it as they will and just keep plodding along, boringly, day to day.”
